# Widget catalog

**Do not edit this file.** It is generated from the `# Widget catalog`
doc block at the top of `crates/enzui-widgets/src/lib.rs` by
`crates/enzui-widgets/tests/contracts/widget_catalog_page.rs`, and the
`docs_widgets_md_is_not_stale` test
(`crates/enzui-widgets/tests/contracts/widget_catalog_page_staleness.rs`)
fails the build if this file and that
block disagree. To change an entry, edit the doc block and regenerate:

```sh
ENZUI_WRITE_WIDGET_DOC=1 cargo wt --test contracts widget_catalog_page
```

This page lists all **240** tier-1 (supported public API) widget
modules, grouped by what you are trying to do. Tier 1 is derived, not
typed: it is every `pub mod` in the crate minus the internal-composition
and audit/probe lists, and `widget_catalog_partitions_tier1` makes a
missing, doubled or phantom entry a hard error.

New to the framework? Read [building-an-app.md](building-an-app.md)
first - it covers the `Message` round-trip, the app shell and
responsiveness. This page answers the other question: *what already
exists*.

Focusable widgets register with the framework focus ring. Enter the event loop
through `enzui_widgets::app_setup::run` to get automatic Tab and Shift+Tab
traversal. Hosts with their own event loop must install traversal explicitly;
`run_with_traversal` selects a custom chord or disables the default binding.
See [building-an-app.md](building-an-app.md) for the application setup route.

## How to read an entry

Each entry names its module, what it is for, and the crate-root imports
it provides:

- **`enz_*`** - the constructor function(s). Where a module offers
several, the one named after the module comes first and the rest are
variants.
- **`Enz*`** - the builder type(s) the constructor returns. You need the
name when a struct field or a function signature has to mention it;
every tier-1 builder type is re-exported at the crate root, so
`enzui_widgets::EnzButton` resolves.
- **source** - the module's own file, linked from its name in each
table below. It resolves on a fresh clone (no `cargo doc` step), and
the module header is the option list and rationale worth reading. To
render the API as HTML instead, run
`cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps` and open
`target/doc/enzui_widgets/<module>/index.html`.

The shape is the same for every widget:

```rust
use enzui_widgets::{enz_badge, enz_button, enz_text};
use iced::Element;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    Save,
}

fn view<'a>() -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let row = iced::widget::row![
        enz_text("Unsaved changes").into_element(),
        enz_badge("draft").into_element(),
        enz_button("Save", Message::Save).into_element(),
    ]
    .spacing(8);

    row.into()
}
```

Prefer a group's container over hand-rolling one: the containers carry
the token wiring and the accessibility semantics that a bare
`iced::widget::container` cannot.

```rust
use enzui_theme::SpaceToken;
use enzui_widgets::banner::BannerTone;
use enzui_widgets::status_dot::StatusKind;
use enzui_widgets::{enz_banner, enz_card, enz_status_dot, enz_text, enz_vstack};
use iced::Element;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    Retry,
}

fn view<'a>() -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let banner = enz_banner("Sync failed")
        .body("The last three changes are still local.")
        .tone(BannerTone::Warning)
        .action_text("Retry")
        .on_action(Message::Retry)
        .into_element();

    let status = enz_status_dot(StatusKind::Warning).into_element();

    enz_card(
        enz_vstack(vec![
            banner,
            iced::widget::row![status, enz_text("3 changes pending").into_element()]
                .spacing(6)
                .into(),
        ])
        .gap(SpaceToken::Sm)
        .into_element(),
    )
    .title("Status")
    .into_element()
}
```

Both blocks above are compiled by the `contracts` integration-test target.
They are marked regions of `crates/enzui-widgets/tests/fixtures/widget_catalog.rs`,
spliced in verbatim, never retyped.

## Naming and imports

Every component in this catalog follows one grammar, so a name tells you what it is:

- **Canonical component module** - the unprefixed `snake_case` *concept* (`text`, `table`, `button`, `image`), never a brand-prefixed or `_widget`-suffixed path.
- **Canonical visual constructor** - prefix-first `enz_snake_case` (`enz_text`, `enz_disabled_button`). The `enz_` marker always comes first, never in the middle.
- **Canonical visual builder / type** - `EnzUpperCamelCase` (`EnzText`, `EnzButton`).
- **Models, policies, controllers, measurements and support helpers** use ordinary Rust names and do **not** acquire an `Enz`/`enz_` marker merely because they support a widget (`TextSize`, `CellCoord`, `ToastHost`, `FileRequest`, lifecycle policies).
- Every canonical tier-1 constructor and every `Enz*` builder type is reachable **both** from its module and from the crate root (`enzui_widgets::enz_button` and `enzui_widgets::button::enz_button` both resolve).
- **Compatibility aliases are not canonical catalog entries.** The historical brand-prefixed module paths (`enz_text`, `enz_table`, `image_widget`, …) and the reversed / bare constructor spellings (`disabled_enz_button`, `revision_text`) keep resolving for existing callers, but they do not appear in this catalog or in `docs/widgets.json`; reach for the canonical spelling in new code.

## Finding a widget by keyword

The group headings answer *what am I trying to do*. The table below
answers the other direction: *I have a name in mind, where did it ship?*
It is an **index**, not an incident log: every tier-1 widget module is
reachable here by at least one intent term that is **not** its own module
name - the term an app author porting from GTK4/Adwaita, SwiftUI, shadcn
or Kirigami would actually type (`segmented control`, `spinbox`, `empty
state`, `snackbar`, `split view`, `data grid`, …). Grep for the term you
were going to type into the file finder and the row here points at the
module that ships it.

Rows cover the terms other design systems use for a widget that ships
under a different name here. `enz_autocomplete_field`, for example, is an
autocomplete dropdown rather than `typeahead`, because
"typeahead" already means the Nautilus type-to-jump feature elsewhere in
this codebase, so an author searching "autocomplete" would not find it


**The flywheel.** If you searched this table for an intent term and did
*not* find your widget, that is a bug in the index, not proof the widget
is missing - add the term you searched for as a new alias row in the same change that resolves it. The index then improves through
use instead of only after an audit.

This is a **checked** table, not free prose:
`keyword_aliases_resolve_to_real_modules` (`tests/contracts/widget_catalog_page_discovery.rs`)
fails the build if any target names a `pub mod` that does not exist;
`every_tier1_module_has_a_non_self_keyword` - the
coverage floor - fails, naming the modules, if any tier-1 module becomes
reachable only by its own name (or by nothing).

Closure-shaped searches are welcome too: `content(|size|)` is the common
spelling for content that needs the shell's resolved width, and the row
below routes it through its prose aliases without requiring a second outer
responsive host.

The widget keeps its own clock and publishes tracks, so the application sends **no per-frame messages** and its view is not rebuilt while the child moves; the render lane moves the recorded child by itself. | `tree view` | [`tree_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tree_view.rs) - the prose name for the keyboard-navigable tree of flattened rows; the intent terms (`tree`, `outline`, `OutlineGroup`) are on its row above. For a folding sidebar *section* use `expander` instead. |
| `window lifecycle` | [`window_lifecycle`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/window_lifecycle.rs) - the prose name for the multi-window exit-policy `iced::Task` binding; the intent terms (`second window`, `multi-window`, `close last window`) are on its row above. |
| `nav split` | [`nav_split`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/nav_split.rs) - the collapse-rule *state* (inline pane / overlay drawer / hidden) for the adaptive navigation shell. For the shell widget itself see the `split view` row (`navigation_split_view`). |
| `collapse search on small screens`, `search collapses to an icon`, `search icon button`, `search popup`, `responsive search`, `narrow search`, `search in a popover`, `expanding search box`, `focus search field id when collapsed`, `routed focus to a collapsed search`, `Ctrl+F opens the collapsed search`, `focus(search_field_id) returns None`, `find_focused reports None for a collapsed search field` | [`search_field`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/search_field.rs) - measured responsive search, **on by default**. It measures whether the field can still do its job against its own assigned width - search glyph + **six wide query characters** + clear slot + the selected size's padding - rather than consulting an app/window breakpoint or requiring the whole placeholder to fit. Verbose placeholder prose continues through the normal ellipsis path at usable widths. Below that content-derived usability threshold it renders one search icon button whose box follows [`TitlebarAffordanceTokens`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toolbar_icon.rs) and whose painted glyph reads the same 16 px [`icon::DEFAULT_ICON_SIZE`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/icon.rs) as its titlebar siblings, independently of the expanded field-prefix ladder. The icon carries the same accessible name and native keyboard shortcut as the input, a non-empty query keeps its selected fill so a hidden filter remains visible, activation expands inline with focus already in the input, and Escape closes and restores focus to the icon. Value and exact caret survive collapse/reopen. **The collapsed field is also addressable by routed focus:** a caller's `iced::advanced::widget::operation::focusable::focus(field_id)` (or a `text_input::*` op) walks the responsive wrapper, reaches the input under the icon, and the wrapper opens synchronously so the next rendered tree carries the expanded `Role::TextInput`. Apps that publish an `.id(..)` on the field keep working after the shipped default collapses their layout width. Use `.responsive(false)` only when the field already lives inside another search surface (for example [`command_palette`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/command_palette.rs)), which owns its own responsive presentation. |
| `masonry`, `masonry grid`, `ragged grid`, `variable height tile grid`, `staggered grid`, `waterfall layout`, `Pinterest layout` | **not a widget - and no framework capability exists**. Nothing in this crate lays out a grid of variable-height tiles the ragged way Pinterest and Adwaita's `AdwWrapLayout` do; [`wrap`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/wrap.rs) is a **fixed-cell** chip/badge inventory (identical cell heights) and [`flow`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/flow.rs) is a flex-wrap **row** container (each row aligns to its tallest child, so tiles do not slot upward into gaps). Neither is masonry, and forcing either into that shape produces a broken thumbnail grid. The searcher who typed `masonry` recorded a **zero** hit in the index (not one wrong hit) so this row exists to say so honestly: if you actually need masonry, write it once as a new tier-1 widget with a tests entry, not per-app. Until then, prefer [`responsive_grid`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/responsive_grid.rs) (equal-height cells with size-class breakpoints), whose visual is what most of these searches actually want. |
| `workspace`, `open folder`, `open a folder as a workspace`, `root folder`, `opened folder`, `workspace root`, `workspace as a place` | **not a widget** - an app concept, not a framework primitive. "Workspace" in an editor-style app is the user-owned root a *host* opens; the framework ships **decoration for one** (`workspace favicon in sidebar` on [`sidebar_row`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/sidebar_row.rs), `workspace section` on [`expander`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/expander/mod.rs)) but no *workspace primitive*. That is on purpose - what "a workspace" is (a directory tree? an untitled project? a saved session?) is app vocabulary, and a framework workspace would either be the intersection (nothing useful) or the union (an untyped soup). For a **sidebar section** grouping a workspace's rows, reach for [`expander`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/expander/mod.rs) with `.hover_scope(HoverScope::Group)`; for a **single workspace row** (name + favicon + right-click), reach for [`sidebar_row`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/sidebar_row.rs) with `.icon_source(..)` and `.on_context(..)`. For the folder tree *inside* an opened workspace, reach for [`tree_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tree_view.rs). Recorded here so a search that ended in zero hits lands on a decision - which of the three near-misses does your case want - rather than in silence. |
| `file watcher`, `watch file`, `reload on change`, `external change`, `file changed on disk`, `stale open file` | **not a widget - the capability is in core**: [`enzui_core::file_watch`](../crates/enzui-core/src/file_watch.rs). For a **bounded set of open documents** - an editor's tabs, the book an app has open, the file the preview pane shows - each file stat's on an `iced::time::every` tick and the outcome is a typed `FileWatchOutcome` ladder (`NoBaseline` / `Unchanged` / `Modified` / `Replaced` / `Deleted` / `Appeared` / `ProbeFailed` / `Superseded`). `Superseded` means a probe from a dropped/reopened watcher, or one older than a completion already applied, arrived late: it is discarded before baseline mutation and never requires attention. Admission is monotone in *completions* (a per-watcher high-water mark), not restricted to the latest issued request, so overlapping probes on a slow backend are not starved. Identity is `(dev, ino) + mtime + ctime + len` on Unix, so an atomic save reports `Replaced` and a same-size in-place write can still be detected when either timestamp advances. After loading a document, seed the identity captured from that open file with `FileWatcher::with_baseline`; an unseeded first probe cannot prove that the file stayed unchanged since the load. `FileWatcher::acknowledge` suppresses the app's **own** save and invalidates older probes. The filesystem backend follows a final symlink to its effective target, treats a dangling link as absent, and reports special targets as `ProbeFailed`. Submit `FileWatcher::prepare_probe()` with `ProbeOp::dispatch` through an application-owned [`enzui_core::blocking_task::BlockingTaskOwner`](../crates/enzui-core/src/blocking_task.rs); an async wrapper alone does not offload `stat(2)`. For event-driven directory membership changes, see the `inotify` row below. |
| `inotify`, `kqueue`, `FSEvents`, `notify-rs`, `watch directory`, `watch a directory`, `filesystem event`, `fs event`, `directory watcher`, `workspace watcher` | [`enzui_core::file_tree_watch`](../crates/enzui-core/src/file_tree_watch/mod.rs) supplies bounded, event-driven directory membership watches, with a native Linux inotify backend. Subscribe to a finite set of visible folders, handle overflow by refreshing listings, and release watches when they are no longer needed. This is not an unbounded recursive workspace watcher. For polling a bounded set of open documents, use [`enzui_core::file_watch`](../crates/enzui-core/src/file_watch.rs). |

Capabilities in **other crates** that a widgets-crate reader will search
for and not find here are listed alongside.

## Composes with

Composition rows name containers and their collaborators. Use these links
to find the widgets needed inside a surface; related module documentation
links collaborators back to their containers. The machine-readable catalog
in `docs/widgets.json` carries the same collaborator arrays in table order.

| widget | composes with | why |
|---|---|---|
| [`title_bar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/title_bar.rs) | [`window_controls`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/window_controls.rs), [`titlebar_icon_group`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/titlebar_icon_group.rs), [`toolbar_icon`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toolbar_icon.rs), [`titlebar_actions`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/titlebar_actions.rs) | A titlebar is five widgets, not one. The band owns ordered slots, the drag region and reserved controls width; it builds [`window_controls`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/window_controls.rs) itself once `on_gesture` is wired. Trailing commands belong in the band's budgeted [`.actions(..)`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/title_bar.rs) slot, never in a pushed standalone [`titlebar_actions`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/titlebar_actions.rs). Read `# Composing a titlebar` in the module header for the layer-by-layer map. |
| [`titlebar_icon_group`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/titlebar_icon_group.rs) | [`toolbar_icon`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toolbar_icon.rs), [`titlebar_actions`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/titlebar_actions.rs) | The cluster **container** for custom composition: variant fill/border, 8 px grouping rhythm, fixed 32 px height, centre alignment and a rounded clip mask. Its children are [`toolbar_icon`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toolbar_icon.rs)s; a standalone [`titlebar_actions`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/titlebar_actions.rs) remains chrome-free and may be wrapped here only outside [`title_bar::EnzTitleBar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/title_bar.rs). This is the exact edge whose absence let an author ship a titlebar with no icon cluster at all. |

[`modal_surface`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/modal_surface.rs) is the container that dialog content sits on; every shipped preset ([`confirm_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/confirm_dialog.rs), [`shortcuts_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/shortcuts_dialog.rs)) builds a surface and hands it to the host as its `dialog` argument. A host with hand-rolled content gets no radius, padding, elevation or close affordance. |
| [`modal_surface`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/modal_surface.rs) | [`capped_dialog_body`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/capped_dialog_body.rs) | A plain surface intentionally accepts arbitrary content and changes no existing geometry. [`section_header`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/section_header.rs) is the *third* job - an 11 px muted caption for a form-group rail - and is what goes **inside** a card body to caption a sub-group; swapping it in as a page heading makes the heading smaller than the body text under it. | [`group_box`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/group_box.rs) | [`card`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/card.rs) | The borderless-by-default tonal group container is presented through [`card`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/card.rs) (surface tokens, rhythm); reach for `card` directly when you need the card's visuals without a titled group. |
| [`tab_pill`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tab_pill.rs) | [`horizontal_scroll_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/horizontal_scroll_view.rs) | A tab strip too wide for its band is not clipped, it *scrolls*: the pill row is wrapped in a [`horizontal_scroll_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/horizontal_scroll_view.rs) with scroll-fade edges so a strip that overflows still reveals the tabs beyond it. |
| [`inline_view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/inline_view_switcher.rs) | [`tab_pill`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tab_pill.rs), [`view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_switcher.rs) | The inline segmented switcher is a row of [`tab_pill`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tab_pill.rs)s - reach for the pill directly for a single-widget selection cue; reach for the switcher when you have a small set of exclusive views to swap. It **is** [`view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_switcher.rs)'s engine under [`SwitcherPolicy::INLINE_SEGMENTED`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_switcher.rs): one page model, one selection/keyboard/a11y owner, two presentation presets. Pick the preset by where the control sits (toolbar chrome vs inline in content), not by which features you need. |
| [`view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_switcher.rs) | [`tab_pill`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tab_pill.rs) | Same shape as [`inline_view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/inline_view_switcher.rs): the segmented row is [`tab_pill`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tab_pill.rs)s; the switcher wraps them with the exclusive-selection routing. |
| [`expander`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/expander/mod.rs) | [`toggle`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toggle.rs) | The disclosure summary carries a [`toggle`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toggle.rs) as its expand/collapse control when the caller asks for a switch (rather than a chevron) - the expander is the container, the toggle is the affordance. |
| [`toggle`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toggle.rs) | [`switch`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/switch.rs) | The public toggle is a [`switch`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/switch.rs) plus the row-shape defaults and the aria-label handling; reach for `switch` directly only when you need the bare pill outside of an operable-toggle context. |
| [`toolbar_icon`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toolbar_icon.rs) | [`icon`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/icon.rs) | The circular icon-only button paints its glyph with an [`icon`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/icon.rs), routed through [`tint_with_status`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/icon.rs) so `hover_color` / `pressed_color` reach the glyph. `icon` is generic (67 consumers) and is otherwise deliberately off the composes-with list - a per-widget edge to it would flood the table. This one edge is specific and justified: an author adding a status-reactive tint to *another* icon-bearing widget needs to learn, from `icon`'s own docs, that [`tint_resolved`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/icon.rs) receives only `&Theme` and so cannot express hover; setting the tokens without the routing change looks exactly like the fix not landing. |

## Choose between siblings

Use this table to choose among widgets that share an intent but differ in
scroll ownership, accessibility semantics, or the surrounding chrome they
provide. Each row links the available siblings and explains when to use them.

| family | siblings | the question that decides | pick |
|---|---|---|---|
| shell | [`app_shell`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/app_shell.rs), [`navigation_split_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/navigation_split_view.rs) | Are you writing the **top-level view of an application**, or an embedded/isolated split whose host owns the titlebar and window chrome? | [`app_shell`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/app_shell.rs) is the default and what all apps use - it owns titlebar, sidebar, content, window chrome, the collapse rule and the drawer semantics in one composition. Reach for [`navigation_split_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/navigation_split_view.rs) **only** for an embedded pane, a secondary window whose host draws the chrome, or a test harness rendering the split in isolation; composing it beside a hand-rolled titlebar and a bare [`window_controls`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/window_controls.rs) cluster duplicates the chrome this family already draws. |
| titlebar-band | [`title_bar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/title_bar.rs), [`header_bar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/header_bar.rs), [`toolbar_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toolbar_view.rs), [`page_header`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/page_header.rs), [`navigation_outlet`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/navigation_outlet.rs) | Is the band the **window titlebar** (drag region, reserved controls, split at the sidebar seam), the **toolbar** above the content pane, the header of a **routed page**, or the outlet of a **navigation stack**? | [`title_bar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/title_bar.rs) is the window band inside [`app_shell`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/app_shell.rs): it owns the drag region and the [`.actions(..)`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/title_bar.rs) budget, and shipping a titlebar with **no icon cluster** by using standalone [`titlebar_actions`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/titlebar_actions.rs) as generic titlebar content is a recorded defect. [`toolbar_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toolbar_view.rs) is the SwiftUI-`.toolbar` port for placement decisions; [`header_bar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/header_bar.rs) is the plain titled bar the others build on. [`page_header`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/page_header.rs) is a **page**'s header with responsive action folding; [`navigation_outlet`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/navigation_outlet.rs) is a **routed** back-button + title + action row. Reach for `header_bar` directly only when you own the placement yourself. |
| segmented-control | [`view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_switcher.rs), [`inline_view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/inline_view_switcher.rs), [`tab_pill`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tab_pill.rs), [`radio_group`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/radio_group.rs) | Are you switching between **whole views/pages**, offering an inline segmented control **within content**, drawing a single **tab pill**, or presenting a semantic **radio-button group** for a form value? | [`view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_switcher.rs) is the toolbar-chrome view-swap. [`inline_view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/inline_view_switcher.rs) is [`view_switcher`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_switcher.rs)'s engine under [`SwitcherPolicy::INLINE_SEGMENTED`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_switcher.rs) - pick the preset by where the control sits (toolbar vs inline), not by which features you need. [`tab_pill`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tab_pill.rs) is a single pill for a one-widget selection cue; hand-rolling a row of pills instead of using a switcher loses the exclusive-selection routing and the keyboard model. [`radio_group`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/radio_group.rs) is the **form-value** exclusive control (the mode-switch role an app once emulated with two buttons), never a view swap: its semantic role is `RadioGroup`, so screen readers hear a group of radios rather than tabs. |
| button-emphasis | [`button`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button.rs), [`confirm_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/confirm_dialog.rs), [`form_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/form_dialog/mod.rs) | Is the button a dialog's or form's **default action**, an ordinary **neutral** action, or the **way out**? | On a [`button`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button.rs), [`ButtonKind::Accent`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button.rs) is the default or suggested action; [`confirm_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/confirm_dialog.rs) and [`form_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/form_dialog/mod.rs) use it for confirm and submit. [`ButtonKind::Primary`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button.rs) is a neutral filled button for an action that is not the default, and on a dialog surface it does not stand out. Cancel and close are [`ButtonKind::Quiet`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button.rs). |
| chat-surfaces | [`chat_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/chat_list.rs), [`chat_transcript`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/chat_transcript.rs) | Do you need a **virtualised, host-scrolled** transcript (long histories, tens of thousands of messages) or a **presentational** transcript column that composes cleanly inside another surface? | [`chat_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/chat_list.rs) is the virtualised list - it has **no self-scrolling mode**, so the `on_scroll` → `update` → `.scroll_offset(..)` round trip is the only route (over 10,000 messages: unwired realises 0..=9 at every offset; wired 120..=134). [`chat_transcript`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/chat_transcript.rs) delegates its scrolling to [`scroll_column`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/scroll_column.rs) with the shared [`tail_follow`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tail_follow.rs) anchor and is what you want for short histories, LLM previews, and any place the host is already inside a scroll container. Both open at the newest message and release the pin when the reader scrolls up; the choice is scroll ownership, not chrome. |
| card-container | [`card`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/card.rs), [`group_box`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/group_box.rs), [`preferences_group`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/preferences_group.rs), [`section_header`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/section_header.rs) | Is this a **discrete entity** with its own identity or actions, a **page section** stacked with other sections, a **settings-rhythm group** of preference rows, or a **caption above a rail of controls**? | [`card`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/card.rs) with `CardTone::Default` (or `Outlined` when the border genuinely separates it from an *adjacent* pane) says *"this is a thing"*; a **page section** is the same widget with `CardTone::Flat` - a bold heading (17 px at baseline text scale), no fill, no border. [`group_box`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/group_box.rs) is the borderless-by-default tonal group presented through [`card`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/card.rs); [`preferences_group`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/preferences_group.rs) is the settings-rhythm specialisation of the same card, flat by default. [`section_header`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/section_header.rs) is the **third** job - an 11 px muted caption for a form-group rail - and it lives inside a card body to caption a sub-group; swapping it in as a page heading makes the heading smaller than the body text under it. A border that appears around every section separates nothing: name what a border separates before adding one. |

## Text and typography

[`enz_text`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text.rs) supplies plain text with the framework's type scale,
semantic weights and tone tokens. This group also contains label/value
pairings, captions, measurement and whole-document renderers; custom text
surfaces keep their own layout and rendering policies.

[`section_header`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/section_header.rs) is a muted caption band (11 logical
pixels at the default scale). For a titled page-section container, use
[`card`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/card.rs)'s Flat tone, whose title publishes a Section heading.

| widget | what it is for | crate-root API |
|---|---|---|
| [`text`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text.rs) | token-driven typography primitive; unpinned families and semantic weights follow application defaults. `font_role` selects a catalog role, `weight_rung` selects a semantic face policy, and `TextShaping` selects Auto or explicit Advanced/Basic shaping. | `enz_text`, `EnzText` |
| [`label`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/label.rs) | the canonical icon + title (+ optional subtitle) label; `enz_label` presets the form shape. | `enz_label`, `EnzLabel` |
| [`icon_label`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/icon_label.rs) | the SwiftUI `Label`-style row **preset** of [`label`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/label.rs): `EnzIconLabel` is an alias for `EnzLabel`. | `enz_icon_label`, `EnzIconLabel` |
| [`labeled_content`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/labeled_content.rs) | form "label \| value" row (or stacked in compact mode). | `enz_labeled_content`, `enz_labeled_content_compact`, `EnzLabeledContent` |
| [`text_pair`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_pair.rs) | single-line leading text + protected trailing metadata. | `enz_text_pair`, `enz_text_pair_element`, `EnzTextPair`, `EnzTextPairElement` |
| [`section_header`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/section_header.rs) | muted all-caps caption band above a form group or sidebar rail (11 logical pixels at the default scale). For a page-section heading, use `card`'s Flat tone with its `HeadingLevel::Section` title. | `enz_section_header`, `EnzSectionHeader` |
| [`streaming_text`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/streaming_text.rs) | wrapping text with a blinking caret while streaming. **Wiring:** the widget owns no clock, so the caret only blinks if the caller flips `.caret_visible(..)` from an `iced::time::every(CARET_HALF_CYCLE)` subscription; with no subscription the indicator renders correctly and never blinks. | `enz_streaming_text`, `EnzStreamingText` |
| [`markdown`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/markdown.rs) | a token-aware Markdown document renderer with bounded parse/render nesting, a flat render adapter, and stack-safe destruction for caller-built trees. | `enz_markdown`, `markdown::enz_markdown_blocks`, `EnzMarkdown` |
| [`reading_pane`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/reading_pane.rs) | long-form document renderer, including an opt-in revision-aware immutable-snapshot path for large chapters. | `enz_reading_pane`, `enz_revisioned_reading_pane`, `EnzReadingPane`, `EnzReadingParagraph`, `EnzRevisionReadingParagraph` |
| [`revision_text`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/revision_text.rs) | identity + monotonic-revision plain text that materializes immutable content only on a cache miss; construct it with [the public constructor](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/revision_text.rs). | `enz_revision_text` |
| [`paged_text_viewer`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/paged_text_viewer.rs) | visible-row viewer for very large random-access UTF-8 text, with virtual line numbers and distinct source-byte / partial line-index status; an overlay scrollbar emits bounded source-byte seeks without indexing the whole document; the row window is derived from the widget's actual allocation and `PagedTextViewportState` publishes it for update-time navigation, and a short terminal frame is bottom-aligned inside the viewer's own body so the host mounts it as one unconditional child. | `enz_paged_text_viewer`, `enz_paged_byte_viewer`, `EnzPagedTextViewer` |
| [`virtual_text_surface`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/virtual_text_surface.rs) | publishes an app's own editor as one editable accessible text node whose contents are served lazily by `enzui_core::virtual_text`, so an assistive technology can read, select and replace at arbitrary offsets in a document too large to publish eagerly. It wraps the editor and changes no pixels; the widget id it publishes is the id the runtime seam resolves to the real `accesskit::NodeId` of the tree the window published. Distinct from [`paged_text_viewer`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/paged_text_viewer.rs), which renders the visible rows of a large read-only document and announces only those rows. | `enz_virtual_text_surface` |
| [`block_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/block_list.rs) | sequence of prose blocks (heading / paragraph / blockquote / list-item / ordered-item / rule / spacer). | `enz_block_list`, `EnzBlock`, `EnzBlockList` |
| [`code_block`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/code_block.rs) | flat-by-default code-snippet display. | `enz_code_block`, `EnzCodeBlock` |
| [`match_ink`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/match_ink.rs) | editor highlighter that resolves readable glyph ink inside a find match, so an accent-filled current match cannot swallow syntax-coloured text. | *not a widget - see module docs* |
| [`text_grid`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_grid.rs) | a single-row dense text grid for TUI-style output. | `enz_text_grid`, `enz_text_grid_shared`, `EnzTextGrid` |
| [`line_number_gutter`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/line_number_gutter.rs) | a line-number gutter that stays aligned under word wrapping. A scrolled wrapped editor must pass the editor-owned first logical line / content-space top through [`GutterConfig::window`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/line_number_gutter.rs), even for a small document: independently shaping the whole prefix and applying a sparse editor offset can put logical line 130 beside label 34/66/77. Pass the same viewport's absolute offset through [`GutterConfig::scroll_offset`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/line_number_gutter.rs), so a responsive re-parent starts at the mapped window instead of zero. The seed applies only to fresh state; the shared `.scroll_id(..)` continues to drive live scrolling. | `enz_line_number_gutter` |
| [`text_measure`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_measure.rs) | font-backed wrapped text height, height-derived line counts, and byte break offsets. | `enz_text_measure`, `enz_text_break_offset_with`, `enz_text_measure_width`, `enz_text_measure_with` |
| [`window_title`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/window_title.rs) | a bold title with an optional muted subtitle. | `enz_window_title`, `EnzWindowTitle` |
| [`wizard`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/wizard.rs) | a step-by-step assistant: the step list, the current page and Cancel, Back, Next or Finish. | `wizard::enz_wizard` |
| [`selection_scope`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/selection_scope.rs) | focusable cross-widget read-only text selection with pointer and shaped keyboard range navigation; only the focused scope owns copy/select/context shortcuts. | `enz_selection_scope`, `selection_scope::enz_selection_row`, `EnzSelectionScope` |

## Buttons and actions

Things the user clicks to *cause* something. [`button`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button.rs) is the
default; the rest are shape variants (round chips for chrome, pills for
suggestions) or containers that arrange several actions.
[`pressable`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/pressable.rs) is the escape hatch when you need
button-like hover/press/selected behaviour on a surface that must not look
like a button.

| widget | what it is for | crate-root API |
|---|---|---|
| [`button`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button.rs) | a styled button component, including [`enz_filter_chip`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button.rs) for compact filters with visible and accessible toggle state. | `enz_button`, `button::enz_button_with`, `enz_disabled_button`, `enz_filter_chip`, `enz_inert_button`, `EnzButton` |
| [`button_group`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/button_group.rs) | action cluster of joined buttons. | `enz_button_group`, `EnzButtonGroup`, `EnzButtonGroupItem` |
| [`link`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/link.rs) | a styled hyperlink component. | `enz_link`, `EnzLink` |
| [`pressable`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/pressable.rs) | a clickable surface with button-like hover/press/selected behaviour, without being a button. | `enz_pressable`, `enz_pressable_maybe`, `EnzPressable` |
| [`clickable`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/clickable.rs) | wraps arbitrary content as a button (role, focus, Enter/Space, hover, minimum hit target). | `enz_clickable`, `enz_clickable_maybe`, `enz_clickable_with_status`, `EnzClickable` |
| [`action_bar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/action_bar.rs) | an action row that folds whole commands into an overflow menu instead of clipping them. **Wiring:** hold the menu state in the app, pass `.overflow_open(..)`, and use the toggle message only for the trigger. Set [`.on_dismiss(..)`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/action_bar.rs) to a distinct message that unconditionally closes the menu; it is published after a row command and for Escape/outside dismissal. For a named `Collector::Kebab`, call [`overflow_focus_restore_operation`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/action_bar.rs) with the prior open state and trigger id when either reducer closes the menu. | `enz_action_bar`, `EnzActionBar` |
| [`toolbar_icon`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toolbar_icon.rs) | circular icon-only button for titlebars / toolbars. `.icon_source(..)` accepts bundled names (tinted) or application SVG/raster artwork (untinted and contained in the glyph box); `.aria_label(..)` is required. | `enz_toolbar_icon`, `EnzToolbarIcon` |
| [`sidebar_toggle_button`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/sidebar_toggle_button.rs) | circular icon-only chip that toggles the sidebar. | `enz_sidebar_toggle_button`, `EnzSidebarToggleButton` |
| [`window_control_button`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/window_control_button.rs) | icon-only round chip for window chrome. | `enz_window_control_button`, `EnzWindowControlButton` |
| [`menu_bar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/menu_bar.rs) | a desktop menu bar (File, Edit, View) built from a menu model, with submenus, F10 and arrow-key navigation, and access keys. | `menu_bar::enz_menu_bar`, `menu_bar::EnzMenuBar` |
| [`mnemonic`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/mnemonic.rs) | access keys: Alt and an underlined letter activate a control (`"_Save"`). |  |
| [`menu_button`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/menu_button.rs) | the controlled menu-button host. | `enz_menu_button`, `enz_kebab_menu_button`, `enz_split_menu_button`, `EnzMenuButton` |

## Text input and forms

Widgets that read a value back out of the user. Each is *controlled*: it
takes the current value or editor content plus a message constructor. The
application applies reported edits; widgets retain interaction state such
as focus and cursor position. The containers at the end of the
group ([`form_layout`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/form_layout.rs),
[`preferences_group`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/preferences_group.rs)) handle label alignment so
rows do not each hand-roll it.

| widget | what it is for | crate-root API |
|---|---|---|
| [`text_field`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_field.rs) | a styled text input component. | `enz_text_field`, `enz_text_field_owned`, `EnzTextField` |
| [`text_area`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs) | multi-line text editor with a standard auto-hidden overlay scrollbar driven by the editor's real scroll metrics (one scroll owner; wrapping on never shows horizontal chrome, while wrapping off shows it only for real horizontal overflow). **Sizing to content:** for an auto-growing composer call [`.auto_grow(min_rows, max_rows)`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs) - it grows one *wrapped row* at a time and then scrolls; do **not** size a box from `Content::line_count`, which counts *logical* `\n` lines and leaves a wrapped paragraph clipped in a one-row box. To measure rows yourself use [`.row_count(width)`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs), which forwards that area's font, size, line height, advanced shaping, and wrapping policy to [`text_measure`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_measure.rs). [`text_area::row_count_at`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs) is the default-font, word-wrapped convenience form. **Slots:** [`.leading(el)`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs) / [`.trailing(el)`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs) reserve an edge slot (trailing bottom-aligned) that shrinks the editor *width* so an inline mic/counter/send never overlaps the text. | `enz_text_area`, `EnzTextArea` |
| [`rich_edit`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/rich_edit.rs) | a rich-text editor with a formatting toolbar; keep a [`RichEditor`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/rich_edit/editor.rs) and read and write HTML. | `enz_rich_edit`, `enz_rich_edit_builder`, `rich_edit::enz_rich_edit_toolbar`, `rich_edit::enz_rich_edit_toolbar_builder`, `EnzRichEdit`, `rich_edit::EnzRichEditToolbar` |
| [`text_float`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_float.rs) | an element floated in a [`text_area`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs) or [`rich_edit`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/rich_edit.rs) document, like an image placed against a paragraph: [`TextFloat`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_float.rs) sits at the top of a line against the left or right edge, the paragraph flows beside it and continues at the full width below, and it scrolls with the text while the content, caret and undo history stay one document. |  |
| [`composer`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/composer.rs) | the chat / prompt input: auto-grow with a row cap, Enter/Shift+Enter, an in-field trailing slot, an action rail, and a send button that swaps to stop on a busy flag. It owns the input **geometry** apps were measuring by hand. | `enz_composer`, `EnzComposer` |

## Navigation and app shell

The chrome around your content: what a window is made of before any of your
own widgets appear. Start at
[`navigation_split_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/navigation_split_view.rs) - it is the adaptive
sidebar/content shell every reference app is built on - then add a
titlebar, header bar and status strip from this group rather than composing
rows by hand, because these carry the drag regions and window-control
semantics a client-side-decorated window needs.

The shell splits in two: [`navigation_split_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/navigation_split_view.rs)
renders, while [`nav_split`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/nav_split.rs) owns the decision of *when* a
sidebar collapses to an overlay drawer. Reach for the widget to build a
layout; read the state module to understand or test the collapse rule.

| [`navigation_split_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/navigation_split_view.rs) | the adaptive navigation shell. | `enz_navigation_split_view`, `EnzNavigationSplitView` |
| [`single_instance`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/single_instance.rs) | one instance per user (`application-dbus`): `SingleInstance::start(app_id)` owns the application or forwards a later launch's files to it; the owner drains them with the task that raises its window. |  |

## Layout and spacing

Arrangement primitives with no visual of their own. They exist so spacing
comes from the token scale instead of magic numbers, and so the responsive
decisions ([`view_that_fits`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/view_that_fits.rs),
[`responsive_grid`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/responsive_grid.rs)) key off *component* width rather
than window width.

## Containers, surfaces and scrolling

Things that give content a background, a border, a radius or a viewport.
[`surface`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/surface.rs) is the unopinionated base (visual only, no imposed
inner layout); [`card`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/card.rs) is the common preset. If content can
exceed its region, wrap it in one of the scroll members rather than letting
it overflow - an unbounded child inside a bounded region is the most common
layout defect.

| [`scroll_column`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/scroll_column.rs) | top-anchored scrollable vertical stack. `.complete_rows(row_height)` retains the parent's actual allocation while limiting paint/input to its largest whole-row inner viewport; `.free_form_viewport()` keeps the ordinary unquantized allocation, and neither policy snaps pixel scroll offsets. | `enz_scroll_column`, `EnzScrollColumn` |
| [`scroll_card`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/scroll_card.rs) | flat scrolling surface with optional border. | `enz_scroll_card`, `EnzScrollCard` |

| [`editor_scrollbar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/editor_scrollbar.rs) | [`enz_editor_scrollbar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/editor_scrollbar.rs) paints the same auto-hidden overlay thumb over a caller-owned, internally-scrolling `iced::widget::text_editor` whose scroll offset the *editor* owns. Reach for it when an app owns its own editor chrome - a distinct font-size ladder, a line-number gutter, a bespoke frame - so it cannot adopt [`text_area`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs) without reshaping its text, yet still needs a scrollbar. It reads the editor's real `scroll_metrics()` and drives an absolute `Action::ScrollTo` through the caller's own reducer, so the editor stays the sole scroll owner; for the standard fully-chromed field use [`text_area`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/text_area.rs), which builds this adapter for you, and when the *caller* owns the offset use [`offset_scrollbar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/offset_scrollbar.rs) instead. | `enz_editor_scrollbar`, `EnzEditorScrollbar` |
| [`tail_follow`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tail_follow.rs) | opens a scroll region at the newest content and follows appends, releasing while the reader is scrolled up. | `enz_tail_follow` |

## Lists, tables and virtualisation

Collections. The virtualised members
([`virtual_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/virtual_list.rs), [`virtual_grid`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/virtual_grid.rs),
[`enz_table`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/table.rs), [`chat_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/chat_list.rs)) realise only
the visible window, so they are what you want past a few hundred rows; the
row widgets are the cells you put inside them.

| widget | what it is for | crate-root API |
|---|---|---|
| [`table`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/table.rs) | a bounded 2D virtualised data grid; `Length::Fill` realization uses the actual allocation, fixed-height bodies reserve only complete row slots, and `TableViewportState` publishes the effective viewport for update-time navigation. `.on_row_activate(..)` makes hover, press and selection one rounded row surface instead of one transient highlight per cell. It requires the default unfrozen layout because split panes cannot honestly expose one row action. | `enz_table`, `EnzTable` |
| [`table_header_cell`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/table_header_cell.rs) | sortable column-header cell. | `enz_table_header_cell`, `EnzTableHeaderCell` |
| [`table_text_cell`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/table_text_cell.rs) | single-line text cell for a data table. | `enz_table_text_cell`, `EnzTableTextCell` |
| [`virtual_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/virtual_list.rs) | a scrolling list that realises only the visible items. Use `.self_scrolling(..)` to synchronize idle scrolling without application messages, or feed `.on_scroll(..)` back through `.scroll_offset(..)`; without either, realization stays at the supplied offset. | `enz_virtual_list`, `enz_virtual_list_variable`, `enz_virtual_list_with_geometry`, `EnzVirtualList` |
| [`virtual_grid`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/virtual_grid.rs) | a model-backed virtual spatial grid for photo, icon and file-thumbnail collections. Use `.self_scrolling(..)` for message-free synchronization, or feed `.on_scroll(..)` back through `.scroll_offset(..)`; without either, realization stays at the supplied offset. | `enz_virtual_grid`, `EnzVirtualGrid` |
| [`file_browser`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/file_browser.rs) | a host-owned listing with per-type icons and natural sort. [`file_browser::FileMetadataColumn`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/file_browser.rs) adds fixed-width host cells to its responsive prefix; [`file_browser::EnzFileBrowser::header_radius`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/file_browser.rs) rounds only the header. | `enz_file_browser`, `EnzFileBrowser` |
| [`tree_view`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tree_view.rs) | a keyboard-navigable, scrolling tree of pre-flattened rows. | `enz_tree_view`, `EnzTreeItem`, `EnzTreeView` |
| [`tree_disclosure`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tree_disclosure.rs) | expand/collapse chevron for tree rows. | `enz_tree_disclosure`, `tree_disclosure::enz_tree_disclosure_lazy`, `EnzTreeDisclosure` |
| [`list_row_surface`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/list_row_surface.rs) | a focusable, keyboard-activatable row surface with hover / pressed / selected / disabled states. Its trailing action can be revealed on hover/focus, or on hover/focus/selection, without ever leaving the layout or the accessibility tree. | `enz_list_row_surface`, `list_row_surface::enz_list_row_surface_lazy`, `EnzListRowSurface` |
| [`preview_row`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/preview_row.rs) | title + trailing + excerpt + footer list row. | `enz_preview_row`, `EnzPreviewRow` |
| [`print_pdf`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/print_pdf.rs) | lay out headings, paragraphs and images on pages and write them as a vector PDF for printing or export. |  |
| [`keyed_column`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/keyed_column.rs) | a column reconciled by key, so a row keeps its state when rows are inserted or removed above it. **Wiring:** `.animate_moves()` slides the rows a change moves, instead of jumping. |  |
| [`reorder_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/reorder_list.rs) | a keyed list with drag-to-reorder. **Wiring:** rows that are themselves clickable need `.drag_through_children(true)`, or the child captures every press and nothing is draggable. | `enz_reorder_list`, `EnzReorderList` |
| [`download_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/download_list.rs) | the view over the core download model. | `enz_download_list`, `enz_download_list_provider`, `EnzDownloadList` |
| [`shortcut_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/shortcut_list.rs) | sectioned list of keyboard-shortcut rows. | `enz_shortcut_list`, `EnzShortcutList` |
| [`chat_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/chat_list.rs) | provider-backed, variable-height virtual chat transcript. **Wiring:** the realised window follows `.scroll_offset(..)`, **not** the inner scrollbar, and this widget has no self-scrolling mode - plumb `.on_scroll(..)` back through `update` into `.scroll_offset(..)` or the same first window is realised forever (measured: messages 0..=9 at every offset). That is the *realisation window*; the **scroll position** is separate and needs no wiring - [`tail_follow`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tail_follow.rs) opens the list at the newest message and follows appended ones by default. **Variable heights:** a height table built from an estimator is a permanent guess - pass `.on_measure(..)` and feed the reported `RowMeasurement`s to `reconcile_measurements`, which corrects the table AND the scroll offset. | `enz_chat_list`, `EnzChatList` |
| [`row_measure`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/row_measure.rs) | report a virtualised row's **intrinsic** height so a variable-height list can correct its guess. This is the producer `VariableHeightModel::apply_measurements` was waiting for; `iced::widget::Sensor::on_resize` reports the *imposed* slot instead, which in a virtual list is the estimate being corrected. | `enz_row_measure`, `EnzRowMeasure` |
| [`chat_transcript`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/chat_transcript.rs) | scrolling surface for chat bubbles. | `enz_chat_transcript`, `EnzChatTranscript` |
| [`chat_bubble`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/chat_bubble.rs) | a rounded chat message bubble. | `enz_chat_bubble`, `EnzChatBubble` |
| [`schedule`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/schedule.rs) | the day/week time-grid surface. | `enz_schedule`, `EnzSchedule` |
| [`carousel`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/carousel/mod.rs) | accessible keyed paging with indicators, prev/next chrome, keyboard paging and optional swipe. | `enz_carousel`, `EnzCarousel` |

## Media and imagery

Pictures, video, audio and the surfaces drawn over them. The playback
widgets are driven by a *snapshot* of media state rather than owning a
decoder, so the same transport bar works over any backend - which is why a
music app should reach for [`media_controls`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/media_controls.rs) instead
of rebuilding one.

## Overlays, menus and dialogs

Anything that renders *above* the page. [`modal_host`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/modal_host.rs) is
the layer that owns modality - scrim, background inertness, Escape,
dismissal routing - and every dialog in this group is presented through it
rather than re-implementing those four things. Menus are the non-modal
half: they dismiss on outside click and do not make the page inert.

| widget | what it is for | crate-root API |
|---|---|---|
| [`modal_host`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/modal_host.rs) | the layer that owns modality and exit motion - scrim, background inertness, Escape, dismissal routing, and visual retention until settlement. **Several dialogs:** [`DialogStack<Key>`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/modal_host.rs) keeps an app's open dialogs and their focus - Escape closes the topmost, closing one closes those over it, `hand_off` replaces one with the next - and renders them over the page with every host level kept mounted. **Exit wiring:** store modal data in [`ModalPresentation`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/modal_host.rs), keep rebuilding its retained value, pass `is_open()` to `EnzModalHost::presentation_open`, and route `on_exit_settled_with` back to `finish_exit(key)`. The exiting subtree is paint-only: no focus stop, dialog role, Escape capture or background inertness. **Focus wiring:** prefer the owned lifecycle [`ModalFocusLifecycle`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/modal_host.rs) - `ModalFocusLifecycle::open(scope_key, invoker)` captures the invoker and returns the initial-focus operation, bind the host to it with `EnzModalHost::scoped_to(&lifecycle)` so the surface scope has one source and cannot drift from the traversal target, and `reduce(event)` answers every `ModalHostEvent` with framework-owned focus work: Tab traversal **scoped to this presentation** (never the unscoped app traversal that leaks focus behind the scrim), invoker restoration at *logical* dismissal (not after exit), and `close_for_host()` for a host-driven/model-unavailable close that must not steal focus. The low-level `initial_focus_operation(scope)` / `scoped_focus_operation(event, scope)` / `restore_focus_operation(event, invoker)` stay public as an escape hatch for a custom host; a host wired with none of them presents a dialog with focus nowhere (measured: zero focused nodes after build). | `enz_modal_host`, `EnzModalHost` |
| [`modal_surface`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/modal_surface.rs) | flat modal container surface. | `enz_modal_surface`, `EnzModalSurface` |
| [`capped_dialog_body`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/capped_dialog_body.rs) | pinned header/action chrome around one scrolling dialog body; derives the body cap from measured chrome. | `enz_capped_dialog_body` |
| [`confirm_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/confirm_dialog.rs) | the canonical "are you sure?" preset over EnzModalHost. | `enz_confirm_dialog`, `EnzConfirmDialog` |
| [`save_changes_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/save_changes_dialog.rs) | the three-action "Save changes before closing?" preset over EnzModalHost. | `enz_save_changes_dialog`, `EnzSaveChangesDialog` |
| [`popover`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/popover.rs) | a floating panel attached to a control or a window-space rectangle, holding any content; dismissed by an outside press or Escape. | `enz_popover`, `EnzPopover` |
| [`about_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/about_dialog.rs) | the application's About dialog: icon, name, version, developer, website and issue links, release notes, credits and legal text, localized. | `about_dialog::enz_about_dialog`, `about_dialog::EnzAboutDialog` |
| [`accordion`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/accordion.rs) | sections of which at most one is open. | `accordion::enz_accordion` |
| [`shortcuts_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/shortcuts_dialog.rs) | keyboard-shortcut help as fill-size content, a card surface, or a hosted modal. | `enz_shortcuts_dialog`, `EnzShortcutsDialog` |
| [`settings_dialog`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/settings_dialog.rs) | the Settings preset over EnzModalHost: dialog → tabs → preference rows, arbitrary pane bodies. | `enz_settings_dialog`, `enz_settings_presentation_for`, `enz_settings_sheet_height`, `EnzSettingsDialog` |
| [`sheet`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/sheet.rs) | [`SheetPresenter`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/sheet/presenter.rs) composes detents, signed drag, viewport/insets, accessible grabber, scroll handoff, and theme-motion settling; route its events through [`SheetPresenter::update`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/sheet.rs). [`enz_sheet`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/sheet/builder.rs) remains the static low-level surface presented over EnzModalHost. | `enz_sheet`, `enz_resizable_sheet`, `EnzSheet` |
| [`full_screen_overlay`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/full_screen_overlay.rs) | dimming scrim + centred content + close button, hosted over EnzModalHost. | `enz_full_screen_overlay`, `EnzFullScreenOverlay` |
| [`menu`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/menu.rs) | elevated menu-surface container. | `enz_menu`, `EnzMenu`, `EnzMenuItem` |
| [`menu_row`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/menu_row.rs) | a single row in a menu / dropdown popup. | `enz_menu_row`, `menu_row::enz_menu_row_maybe`, `menu_row::enz_menu_row_maybe_with`, `enz_menu_separator`, `menu_row::enz_menu_separator_builder`, `EnzMenuRow` |
| [`context_menu_host`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/context_menu_host.rs) | turns a right-click invocation into a positioned, navigable, dismissible menu. [`ContextMenu<Target, Command>`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/context_menu_host.rs) is the usual way in: open it on a row with typed [`ContextMenuItem<Command>`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/context_menu_host.rs)s, mount it with `host(page, ..)`, and `update` hands back `(target, command)` with focus returned to the row. | `enz_context_menu_host`, `enz_optional_point_context_menu_host`, `enz_point_context_menu_host`, `EnzContextMenuHost` |
| [`context_target`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/context_target.rs) | right-click capture surface for context menus. | `enz_context_target`, `context_target::enz_context_target_msg`, `EnzContextTarget` |
| [`crash_notice`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/crash_notice.rs) | the start-up banner saying the app crashed last time and a report was saved. | `crash_notice::enz_crash_notice` |
| [`positioned_overlay`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/positioned_overlay.rs) | places a surface at an app-supplied point, clamped to the viewport, reporting caused outside-press or Escape dismissal without making the page inert. | `enz_positioned_overlay`, `enz_positioned_overlay_with_cause`, `EnzPositionedOverlay` |
| [`tooltip`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/tooltip/mod.rs) | a styled tooltip wrapper. | `enz_tooltip`, `enz_fade_tooltip`, `tooltip::enz_tooltip_bubble`, `enz_tooltip_bubble_opacity`, `enz_tooltip_with_delay`, `enz_tooltip_with_tokens` |
| [`file_chooser`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/file_chooser.rs) | the (`portal-dbus`-gated) seam to the XDG Desktop Portal file chooser, with an opt-in in-app fallback for hosts without one. **Wiring:** `FileRequest::start` only *opens* the request - the caller must also return [`completion_subscription`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/file_chooser.rs) from `App::subscription` and call [`pump`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/file_chooser.rs) when it wakes, or the chooser is presented and its outcome never arrives. That subscription is **event-driven and pending-gated**: it wakes once per portal event, so do not drive `pump` from `window::frames()` or an `iced::time::every` tick - a frame-sourced portal tick asks for work on every compositor frame while a dialog is open, which is the settled-redraw defect class. | *not a widget - see module docs* |

## Feedback and progress

Telling the user what happened or what is happening. The tone-carrying
members ([`banner`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/banner.rs), [`toast`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toast.rs),
[`status_dot`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/status_dot.rs)) publish accessibility live-region roles
keyed off tone, so an assistive technology announces a warning with the
right urgency without any extra wiring.

| widget | what it is for | crate-root API |
|---|---|---|
| [`banner`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/banner.rs) | inline status banner (title + body + tone + optional action + optional dismiss). The default leading glyph is the filled tone chip - the look every existing caller already ships. `EnzBanner::badge_style(BannerBadgeStyle::Bare)` opts into a tone-inked glyph on the banner's own surface, for a banner whose surroundings already carry the tone (for example, mounted through `EnzAppShell::notifications`). Durable actionable status belongs in `EnzAppShell::notifications` rather than hand-mounted in an app's content column. | `enz_banner`, `EnzBanner` |
| [`toast`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toast.rs) | transient toast surface (a single toast's chrome; the dismissal story lives in its host, [`toast_host`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toast_host.rs)). | `enz_toast`, `EnzToast` |
| [`toast_host`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toast_host.rs) | the app-facing controller a toast is queued through: auto-dismiss timers, stacking, coalescing, the overflow/waiting budget, and the one live region that announces the message it is showing. You drive `ToastHost` from `update` the way you drive `file_chooser`; its element-producing entry point is [`enz_toast_layer`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/toast_host.rs), which places the mounted host bottom-centre over the presentation without re-parenting it with an optional bottom inset for an app whose own chrome occupies that edge. | `enz_toast_layer`, `enz_toast_overlay` |
| [`notice_stack`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/notice_stack.rs) | notices about the app's own condition that stay while their cause holds, as a column of toasts that speaks once. | `enz_notice_stack`, `EnzNotice`, `EnzNoticeStack` |
| [`notification_inbox`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/notification_inbox.rs) | the in-app list of past notifications, unread marked, dismissible, with Clear All. | `notification_inbox::enz_notification_inbox` |
| [`activity_surface`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/activity_surface.rs) | the persistent operation-activity status: what the app is doing right now, contributed by every provider into one [`enzui_core::operation_activity::ActivityCenter`](../crates/enzui-core/src/operation_activity.rs) and placed by the shell (`EnzAppShell::activity`) at the sidebar's bottom, as one compact status row by default, or, with the sidebar closed, bottom-left over the content as the detailed panel. Dimensionless fractional completion is shown and announced as an operation percentage; finite input clamps to 0–100%, non-finite input becomes indeterminate, homogeneous fractional operations aggregate with equal operation weight, and mixed units never fabricate a total. Its keyboard/AT-reachable `+N more` action receives an [`ActivityOverflowTarget`](../crates/enzui-core/src/operation_activity.rs) derived from the actual hidden rows, so mixed providers cannot silently route to one provider's panel. A toast leaves; this stays while the work does. | `enz_activity_surface`, `EnzActivitySurface` |
| [`status_dot`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/status_dot.rs) | compact semantic status indicator. | `enz_status_dot`, `EnzStatusDot` |
| [`status_page`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/status_page.rs) | centred empty-state hero view. | `enz_status_page`, `EnzStatusPage` |
| [`spinner`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/spinner.rs) | rotating 8-dot indeterminate loader. | `enz_spinner`, `EnzSpinner` |

| [`frame_clock`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/frame_clock.rs) | wrap any element so it self-animates from frame timestamps, with no app-side tick and no per-frame `view()` rebuild. | `enz_frame_clock`, `EnzFrameClock` |
| [`progress_bar`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/progress_bar.rs) | a styled progress indicator. | `enz_progress_bar`, `enz_progress_bar_sampled`, `EnzProgressBar` |
| [`gauge`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/gauge.rs) | a circular, token-driven gauge showing a value within a range. | `enz_gauge`, `enz_gauge_sampled`, `EnzGauge` |

## Drag and drop

Two hosts you wrap *around* a drag surface. Cross-list dragging and
edge-auto-scrolling are the parts that cannot live inside a single list
widget, which is why they are separate hosts rather than options on
[`reorder_list`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/reorder_list.rs).

| widget | what it is for | crate-root API |
|---|---|---|
| [`drag_drop_host`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/drag_drop_host.rs) | the host that owns one drag session across collections, paints source and target feedback confined to the registering surface in an explicit overlay layer above child/sidebar content, and publishes the grab/grabbing pointer shape a deferred collection cannot. | `enz_drag_drop_host`, `EnzDragDropHost` |
| [`drag_item_surface`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/drag_item_surface.rs) | bounded keyed virtual row/grid registration for onto-item and current-location drops. | `enz_drag_item_surface`, `EnzDragItemSurface` |
| [`drag_autoscroll_host`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/drag_autoscroll_host.rs) | wires auto-scrolling into a real drag path. | `enz_drag_autoscroll_host`, `EnzDragAutoScrollHost` |
| [`file_drag`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/file_drag.rs) | reusable native file and MIME-data sources for rows, thumbnails and attachments; stable ownership keys, bounded selections, pointer/touch thresholds, optional previews and destination completion callbacks. | `file_drag::enz_data_drag_source`, `file_drag::enz_file_drag_source`, `file_drag::enz_file_drag_source_with`, `file_drag::EnzFileDragSource` |
| [`file_drop`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/file_drop.rs) | MIME-aware drop regions with hover feedback and deferred completion; `enz_data_drop_target` receives caller-selected MIME data. Files dragged in from a file manager or another app: wrap a region in `enz_file_drop_target(content, on_drop)` and the dropped paths arrive as one message, through the native drag service `app_setup::run` installs. Text fields keep taking dropped text. | `file_drop::enz_data_drop_target`, `file_drop::enz_file_drop_target`, `file_drop::enz_file_drop_target_with_receipt`, `file_drop::EnzFileDropTarget` |
| [`zoom_wheel`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/zoom_wheel.rs) | Ctrl+wheel zooms the wrapped view instead of scrolling it: one step per notch, touchpad deltas accumulated, at most one step per event. | `enz_zoom_wheel`, `EnzZoomWheel` |

## Decoration and effects

Purely visual wrappers. [`elevation`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/elevation.rs) is the one to prefer:
it takes a semantic 0–5 level and resolves the shadow from the theme, so
two widgets at the same level match. Hand-written `iced::Shadow` values do
not.

| widget | what it is for | crate-root API |
|---|---|---|
| [`elevation`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/elevation.rs) | semantic elevation wrapper with 0-5 shadow levels. | `enz_elevation`, `EnzElevation` |
| [`glow`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/glow.rs) | coloured glow (halo) around content. | `enz_glow`, `EnzGlow` |
| [`gradient_background`](../crates/enzui-widgets/src/gradient_background.rs) | configurable linear-gradient surface. | `enz_gradient_background`, `EnzGradientBackground` |

## What is not on this page

The crate declares 315 `pub mod`s; 240 of them are tier 1 and listed
above. The remainder are **internal-composition** modules (public only so
widgets in this crate and the probe can compose them) and **audit/probe**
modules (they power the test and A/B harness). Both lists, and the reason
each exists, are in the § Export / alias / deprecation boundary section of
the crate rustdoc. Their surface is unstable - do not depend on it.
